title: Concern about bulk integration PRs and affiliation disclosure
body:
I'm the maintainer of [YouDub-webui](https://github.com/liuzhao1225/YouDub-webui). I'm concerned about repeated LiteLLM integration PRs across separate projects, including ours, where existing OpenAI-compatible routing already works and the need for an additional SDK layer needs justification.

Our [archived sample](https://github.com/liuzhao1225/litellm-integration-supply-chain-review/blob/7fef57f041ab6d81da314cfa9f9a08fa3432ba69/PR-INDEX.md) records **49 PRs by prodmanpd across 49 projects**: 22 Python SDK integrations and 27 proxy-compatible integrations. Proxy-only changes do not automatically install the Python SDK.

In [YouDub #130](https://github.com/liuzhao1225/YouDub-webui/pull/130), the [reviewed commit](https://github.com/liuzhao1225/YouDub-webui/commit/1add1b6d90795ddc222c3f5021305a2e8d953a17) moves `litellm>=1.89.0,<2.0.0` into default requirements while the description still calls it optional. The allowed range also extends beyond the author's stated 1.99.0 tests. These mismatches and the repeated integrations raise dependency and transparency concerns for me.

The author's [Chartbrew explanation](https://github.com/chartbrew/chartbrew/pull/365#issuecomment-5207856315) cites teams using existing gateways, which is a plausible use case. **Could LiteLLM/BerriAI clarify whether these contributions are independent, sponsored, or coordinated with the project?** Could contributors document the downstream need, any relevant affiliation, and the actual installation/test boundary?

LiteLLM's [confirmed March 2026 compromise of 1.82.7/1.82.8](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026) makes transparent dependency decisions particularly important. Our review has **not established poisoning of 1.100.0 or 1.101.0rc1, or contributor involvement in an attack**. Evidence, counterexamples and unresolved questions are preserved in the [investigation repository](https://github.com/liuzhao1225/litellm-integration-supply-chain-review).
